title: Count Excellent Pairs
description: You are given a 0-indexed positive integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`. A pair `(nums[i], nums[j])` is excellent if `bits(nums[i] OR nums[j]) + bits(nums[i] AND nums[j]) >= k`. Return number of distinct excellent pairs.
input_format: First line contains `n` and `k`. Second line contains `n` integers.
hints: Key identity: `bits(a OR b) + bits(a AND b) = bits(a) + bits(b)`.
Remove duplicates from `nums` since distinct values define pairs.
Sort set bit counts and use binary search to count valid partners.

reference_solution:
import sys, bisect
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    nums = list(set([int(x) for x in data[2:2+n]]))
    bit_counts = sorted([bin(x).count('1') for x in nums])
    ans = 0
    total = len(bit_counts)
    for c in bit_counts:
        needed = k - c
        idx = bisect.bisect_left(bit_counts, needed)
        ans += (total - idx)
    print(ans)
